6189.text: The value of $c$ of the Lagrange's mean value theorem for $f(x)=\sqrt{x^2-x}, x \in[1,4]$ is
6189.sol:
We have,
$\begin{aligned} & f(x)=\sqrt{x^2-x}, x \in[1,4] \Rightarrow f(1)=\sqrt{1-1}=0 \\ & f(4)=\sqrt{16-4}=\sqrt{12}=2 \sqrt{3} \Rightarrow f^{\prime}(c)=\frac{2 c-1}{2 \sqrt{c^2-c}}\end{aligned}$
By Lagrange's mean value theorem
$f^{\prime}(c)=\frac{f(b)-f(a)}{b-a}\frac{2 c-1}{2 \sqrt{c^2-c}}=\frac{f(4)-f(1)}{4-1}=\frac{2 \sqrt{3}-0}{3}\Rightarrow \frac{2 c-1}{2 \sqrt{c^2-c}}=\frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}\Rightarrow \quad \sqrt{3}(2 c-1)=4 \sqrt{c^2-c} \Rightarrow 3(2 c-1)^2=16 c^2-16 c\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow 3\left(4 c^2-4 c+1\right)=16 c^2-16 c \\ & \Rightarrow 12 c^2-12 c+3=16 c^2-16 c \Rightarrow 4 c^2-4 c-3=0 \\ & \Rightarrow(2 c-3)(2 c+1)=0 \Rightarrow c=3 / 2 \in(1,4)\end{aligned}\therefore \quad c=3 / 2$

Let $\mathrm{t}=4^2\mathrm{dt}=24 \mathrm{du}=\frac{-2}{3} \int \frac{\mathrm{du}}{(1+4)(1-4)}=\left(\frac{-2}{3}\right)\left[\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{1+4} \mathrm{du}+\frac{1}{2} \int \frac{1}{1-4} \mathrm{du}\right]\begin{aligned} & =\frac{-1}{3}\left[\int \frac{1}{1+4} \mathrm{du}+\int \frac{1}{1-4} \mathrm{du}\right]+\mathrm{c} \\ & =\frac{-1}{3}\left[\log _{\mathrm{e}}|1+4|-\log _{\mathrm{e}}|1-4|\right]+\mathrm{c} \\ & =\frac{-1}{3}\left[\log _{\mathrm{e}}|1+\sqrt{\mathrm{t}}|-\log _{\mathrm{e}}|1-\sqrt{\mathrm{t}}|\right]+\mathrm{c} \\ & =\frac{-1}{3}\left[\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left|1+\sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^3}\right|-\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left|1-\sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^3}\right|\right]+\mathrm{c} \\ & =\frac{1}{3}\left[-\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left|1+\sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^3}\right|+\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left|1-\sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^3}\right|\right]+\mathrm{c}\end{aligned}=\frac{1}{3}\left[\log _{\mathrm{e}}\left|\frac{1+\sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^3}}{1+\sqrt{1-\mathrm{x}^3}}\right|\right]+\mathrm{c}\Rightarrow f(x)=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-x^3}}{1+\sqrt{1-x^3}} \Rightarrow f\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{1-\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{8}}}{1+\sqrt{1-\frac{1}{8}}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{1-\sqrt{\frac{7}{8}}}{1+\sqrt{\frac{7}{8}}}=\frac{\sqrt{8}-\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{8}+\sqrt{7}}\Rightarrow \mathrm{f}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)=\frac{\sqrt{8}-\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{8}+\sqrt{7}}$

11608.sol:
We have,
\(x=\frac{1}{5}+\frac{1 \cdot 3}{5 \cdot 10}+\frac{1 \cdot 3 \cdot 5}{5 \cdot 10 \cdot 15}+\ldots\)
Comparing expression with,
\((1+y)^n=\frac{1+n y}{1 !}+\frac{n(n-1)}{2 !} y^2+\ldots .\)
we get,
\(n y=\frac{1}{5}, \frac{n(n-1)}{2 \cdot 1} \cdot y^2=\frac{1 \cdot 3}{5 \cdot 10}\)
Solving we get,
\(y=-\frac{2}{5} \text{ and } n=-\frac{1}{2}\)
So,
\($\begin{array}{ll}
x=(1+y)^n-1 \\
\Rightarrow & x=\left(1-\frac{2}{5}\right)^{-\frac{1}{2}}-1=\sqrt{\frac{5}{3}}-1
\end{array}$
So, \(\quad 3 x^2+6 x\)
\(\begin{aligned}
& =3\left(\sqrt{\frac{5}{3}}-1\right)^2+6\left[\left(\sqrt{\frac{5}{3}}\right)-1\right] \\
& =3\left(\frac{5}{3}+1-2 \sqrt{\frac{5}{3}}\right)+6 \sqrt{\frac{5}{3}}-6 \\
& =5+3-6=2
\end{aligned}\)

19484.subject: Chemistry
19484.text: Which one of the following is the major product formed when the given reaction occurs?
19484.sol:
The reaction involves the cleavage of an ether and the hydrohalogenation of an alkene with excess concentrated HI.

First, the ether linkage $Ar-O-CH_2CH_3$ is cleaved by HI. The oxygen atom is protonated, and the iodide ion attacks the less sterically hindered alkyl group (CH_2CH_3$) via an $S_N2$ mechanism, resulting in the formation of a phenol (Ar-OH$) and ethyl iodide (CH_3CH_2I$).

Second, the alkene group $-CH=CH_2$ attached to the benzene ring undergoes electrophilic addition with HI. According to Markovnikov's rule, the proton (H^+$) adds to the terminal carbon (CH_2$) to form a more stable benzylic carbocation (Ar-CH^{+}-CH_3$), which is stabilized by resonance with the benzene ring. Subsequently, the iodide ion (I^-$) attacks this carbocation to form the product $Ar-CH(I)-CH_3$.

Combining these two processes, the final product is 4-(1-iodoethyl)phenol. This corresponds to the structure where the hydroxyl group is attached to the benzene ring and the 1-iodoethyl group is at the para position.

Answer:

19787.subject: Chemistry
19787.text: Find the correct order of $\mathrm{C}-\mathrm{O}$ bond length among $\mathrm{CO}, \mathrm{CO}_{3}^{2-}, \mathrm{CO}_{2}$.
19787.sol:
The bond length is inversely proportional to the bond order of the molecule or ion.

For $\mathrm{CO}$, the Lewis structure is $:C \equiv O:$, which gives a bond order of $3$.

For $\mathrm{CO}_{2}$, the structure is $O=C=O$, which gives a bond order of $2$.

For $\mathrm{CO}_{3}^{2-}$, the resonance structures result in a bond order of $\dfrac{4}{3} \approx 1.33$.

Comparing the bond orders: $3 > 2 > 1.33$.

Since bond length is inversely proportional to bond order, the order of bond lengths is $\mathrm{CO} < \mathrm{CO}_{2} < \mathrm{CO}_{3}^{2-}$.

Answer: $\mathrm{CO} < \mathrm{CO}_{2} < \mathrm{CO}_{3}^{2-}$

21099.subject: Mathematics
21099.text: The coefficient of $x^{10}$ in the expansion of $1+(1+x)+\ldots+(1+x)^{20}$ is
21099.sol:
The given expression is a geometric series with first term $a = 1$, common ratio $r = (1+x)$, and number of terms $n = 21$.

The sum of the series is $S = a \dfrac{r^n - 1}{r - 1} = 1 \times \dfrac{(1+x)^{21} - 1}{(1+x) - 1} = \dfrac{(1+x)^{21} - 1}{x}$.

We need the coefficient of $x^{10}$ in the expansion of $S = \dfrac{(1+x)^{21} - 1}{x}$.

This is equivalent to finding the coefficient of $x^{11}$ in the expansion of $(1+x)^{21} - 1$.

The general term in the expansion of $(1+x)^{21}$ is given by ^{21}C_{r} x^{r}$.

For $r = 11$, the term is ^{21}C_{11} x^{11}$.

Since the constant term $-1$ does not affect the coefficient of $x^{11}$, the coefficient of $x^{11}$ in $(1+x)^{21} - 1$ is ^{21}C_{11}$.

Therefore, the coefficient of $x^{10}$ in the original expression is ^{21}C_{11}$.

Answer: $\binom{21}{11}$

21116.subject: Mathematics
21116.text: Equation of a circle whose area is 154 sq units and having $2 x-3 y+12=0$ and $x+4 y-5=0$ as diameters is
21116.sol:
The area of the circle is given as $A = \pi r^2 = 154$.

Using $\pi = \dfrac{22}{7}$, we have $\dfrac{22}{7} r^2 = 154$, which implies $r^2 = 154 \times \dfrac{7}{22} = 7 \times 7 = 49$. Thus, $r = 7$.

The center of the circle is the intersection of the two diameters $2x - 3y + 12 = 0$ and $x + 4y - 5 = 0$.

From the second equation, $x = 5 - 4y$. Substituting this into the first equation:

$2(5 - 4y) - 3y + 12 = 0$

$10 - 8y - 3y + 12 = 0$

$22 - 11y = 0 \Rightarrow y = 2$.

Substituting $y = 2$ back into $x = 5 - 4y$:

$x = 5 - 4(2) = 5 - 8 = -3$.

The center of the circle is $(-3, 2)$.

The equation of a circle with center $(h, k)$ and radius $r$ is $(x - h)^2 + (y - k)^2 = r^2$.

Substituting $h = -3$, $k = 2$, and $r^2 = 49$:

$(x + 3)^2 + (y - 2)^2 = 49$

$x^2 + 6x + 9 + y^2 - 4y + 4 = 49$

$x^2 + y^2 + 6x - 4y + 13 - 49 = 0$

$x^2 + y^2 + 6x - 4y - 36 = 0$.

Answer: $x^2+y^2+6 x-4 y-36=0$

21215.sol:
The given function is $f(x) = |x| + |x - 1|$.

We can redefine the function as a piecewise function:

$f(x) = \begin{cases} -x - (x - 1) = -2x + 1, & x < 0 \\ x - (x - 1) = 1, & 0 \le x < 1 \\ x + (x - 1) = 2x - 1, & x \ge 1 \end{cases}$

Checking differentiability at $x = 0$:
Left Hand Derivative (LHD) $= \lim_{x \to 0^-} f'(x) = -2$
Right Hand Derivative (RHD) $= \lim_{x \to 0^+} f'(x) = 0$
Since LHD \neq RHD, $ f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 0$.

Checking differentiability at $x = 1$:
Left Hand Derivative (LHD) $= \lim_{x \to 1^-} f'(x) = 0$
Right Hand Derivative (RHD) $= \lim_{x \to 1^+} f'(x) = 2$
Since LHD \neq RHD, $ f(x)$ is not differentiable at $x = 1$.

Therefore, the function is neither differentiable at $x = 0$ nor at $x = 1$.

Answer: Neither differentiable at $x = 0$ nor $x = 1$

21219.subject: Mathematics
21219.text: The function $f(x)=\left\{\begin{array}{c}\dfrac{|x|}{x}, \text{ if } x \neq 0 \\ 0, \text{ if } x=0\end{array}\right.$ is discontinuous at
21219.sol:
The function is defined as $f(x) = \dfrac{|x|}{x}$ for $x \neq 0$ and $f(0) = 0$.

For $x > 0$, $|x| = x$, so $f(x) = \dfrac{x}{x} = 1$.

For $x < 0$, $|x| = -x$, so $f(x) = \dfrac{-x}{x} = -1$.

Evaluating the limits at $x = 0$:

Left hand limit: $\lim_{x \to 0^{-}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 0^{-}} (-1) = -1$.

Right hand limit: $\lim_{x \to 0^{+}} f(x) = \lim_{x \to 0^{+}} (1) = 1$.

Since the left hand limit and right hand limit are not equal, the limit $\lim_{x \to 0} f(x)$ does not exist. Therefore, the function is discontinuous at $x = 0$.

Answer: $x=0$

22113.text:
If two vertices of a triangle are $(3,-2)$ and $(-2,3)$ and its orthocentre is $(-6,1)$.
Then the difference between ordinate and abscissa of the third vertex of the triangle is
22113.sol:
Let the vertices of the triangle be $A(3, -2)$, $B(-2, 3)$, and $C(x, y)$. The orthocentre $H$ is given as $(-6, 1)$.

The slope of $BC$ is $m_{BC} = \dfrac{y - 3}{x - (-2)} = \dfrac{y - 3}{x + 2}$. Since $AH \perp BC$, the slope of $AH$ is $m_{AH} = \dfrac{1 - (-2)}{-6 - 3} = \dfrac{3}{-9} = -\dfrac{1}{3}$.

The condition $m_{AH} \times m_{BC} = -1$ implies $\left(-\dfrac{1}{3}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{y - 3}{x + 2}\right) = -1$, which simplifies to $\dfrac{y - 3}{x + 2} = 3$, so $y - 3 = 3x + 6$, or $3x - y + 9 = 0$.

The slope of $AC$ is $m_{AC} = \dfrac{y - (-2)}{x - 3} = \dfrac{y + 2}{x - 3}$. Since $BH \perp AC$, the slope of $BH$ is $m_{BH} = \dfrac{1 - 3}{-6 - (-2)} = \dfrac{-2}{-4} = \dfrac{1}{2}$.

The condition $m_{BH} \times m_{AC} = -1$ implies $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right) \times \left(\dfrac{y + 2}{x - 3}\right) = -1$, which simplifies to $\dfrac{y + 2}{x - 3} = -2$, so $y + 2 = -2x + 6$, or $2x + y - 4 = 0$.

Solving the system of equations $3x - y = -9 and 2x + y = 4$:

Adding the two equations gives $5x = -5$, so $x = -1$.

Substituting $x = -1$ into $2x + y = 4$ gives $2(-1) + y = 4$, so $y = 6$.

The third vertex $C$ is $(-1, 6)$. The difference between the ordinate and the abscissa is $y - x = 6 - (-1) = 7$.

Answer: $7$

23433.subject: Physics
23433.text: A point marked on a ring of radius 2 cm is in contact with a horizontal plane. Now the ring is rolled forward half a revolution along the positive X - direction. Then the angle made by the displacement vector of the point with the X - axis is:
23433.sol:
Let the radius of the ring be $R = 2$ cm. Initially, the point is at the origin $(0, 0)$ in contact with the horizontal plane (X-axis).

The ring rolls forward by half a revolution. The distance moved by the center of the ring is $d = R \times \theta_{rot} = R \times \pi = 2\pi$.

After half a revolution, the center of the ring is at $(2\pi, 2)$. The point, which was initially at the bottom, is now at the top of the ring. The coordinates of the point after half a revolution are $(2\pi, 2R) = (2\pi, 4)$.

The displacement vector $\vec{S}$ of the point from its initial position $(0, 0)$ to its final position $(2\pi, 4)$ is $\vec{S} = (2\pi - 0)\hat{i} + (4 - 0)\hat{j} = 2\pi\hat{i} + 4\hat{j}$.

The angle $\theta$ made by the displacement vector with the X-axis is given by $\tan \theta = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \dfrac{4}{2\pi} = \dfrac{2}{\pi}$.

Therefore, $\theta = \tan ^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right)$.

Answer: $\theta=\tan ^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2}{\pi}\right)$

25802.subject: Mathematics
25802.text:
Let $a, b, c$ be positive integers in arithmetic progression such that the equation
$ax^2 + bx + c = 0$
has only integer solutions.
Then which of the following statements is (are) TRUE ?
options: $c - b$ is an integer multiple of $a$
Both the roots of the equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ are odd integers
If $b = 8$, then $x = 3$ is a root of the equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$
25802.sol:
Given $a, b, c$ are in arithmetic progression, we have $2b = a + c$.

Let the integer roots of the equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ be $\alpha$ and $\beta$.

Sum of the roots is $\alpha + \beta = -\dfrac{b}{a}$ and product of the roots is $\alpha \beta = \dfrac{c}{a}$.

Dividing the arithmetic progression condition by $a$, we get:

$\dfrac{2b}{a} = 1 + \dfrac{c}{a}$

Substituting the sum and product of the roots:

$-2(\alpha + \beta) = 1 + \alpha \beta$

$\alpha \beta + 2\alpha + 2\beta + 1 = 0$

Adding $3$ to both sides to factorize:

$\alpha \beta + 2\alpha + 2\beta + 4 = 3$

$(\alpha + 2)(\beta + 2) = 3$

Since $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are integers, $(\alpha + 2)$ and $(\beta + 2)$ must be integer factors of $3$. The possible pairs are $(1, 3)$, $(3, 1)$, $(-1, -3)$, and $(-3, -1)$.

If $(\alpha + 2, \beta + 2) = (1, 3)$ or $(3, 1)$, the roots are $-1$ and $1$. The sum of the roots is $0$, which implies $b = 0$. This is rejected because $b$ is a positive integer.

If $(\alpha + 2, \beta + 2) = (-1, -3)$ or $(-3, -1)$, the roots are $-3$ and $-5$. The sum of the roots is $-8$, which implies $-\dfrac{b}{a} = -8 \Rightarrow b = 8a$.

The product of the roots is $15$, which implies $\dfrac{c}{a} = 15 \Rightarrow c = 15a$.

Since $a$ is a positive integer, $b = 8a$ and $c = 15a$ are also positive integers. The roots of the equation are always $-3$ and $-5$.

Evaluating the given statements:

$c - b = 15a - 8a = 7a$, which is an integer multiple of $a$.

The roots are $-3$ and $-5$, both of which are odd integers.

If $c = 15$, then $15a = 15 \Rightarrow a = 1$. Consequently, $b = 8(1) = 8$. Thus, $ab = 1 \times 8 = 8$.

If $b = 8$, then $8a = 8 \Rightarrow a = 1$. The roots are $-3$ and $-5$, so $x = 3$ is not a root.

Answer: $c - b$ is an integer multiple of $a$; Both the roots of the equation $ax^2 + bx + c = 0$ are odd integers; If $c = 15$, then $ab = 8$

25960.text:
Let $\vec{w}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2 \hat{k}$, and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{u}}$ and $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}$ be two vectors such that $\vec{u} \times \vec{v}=\vec{w}$ and $\vec{v} \times \vec{w}=\vec{u}$. Let $\alpha, \beta, \gamma$ and $t$ be real numbers such that $\vec{u}=\alpha \hat{i}+\beta \hat{j}+\gamma \hat{k},-t \alpha+\beta+\gamma=0, \alpha-t \beta+\gamma=0$, and $\alpha+\beta-t \gamma=0$. Match each entry in List-I to the correct entry in List-II and choose the correct option.
LIST - I LIST - II
(P) $|\vec{v}|^2$ is equal to (1) 0
(Q) If $\alpha=\sqrt{3}$,then $\gamma^2$ is equal to (2) 1
(R) If $\alpha=\sqrt{3}$,then $(\beta+\gamma)^2$ is equal to (3) 2
(S) If $\alpha=\sqrt{2}$,then $t+3$ is equal to (4) 3
(5) 5
25960.sol:
$\begin{array}{lll}\vec{u} \times \vec{v}=\vec{w} & \vec{u} \perp \vec{v} & \vec{u} \perp \vec{w} \\ \vec{v} \times \vec{w}=\vec{u} & \vec{v} \perp \vec{w} & \end{array} \begin{aligned} & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{w}}=\hat{\mathrm{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}-2 \hat{\mathrm{k}} \\ & \overrightarrow{\mathrm{u}}=\alpha \hat{\mathrm{i}}+\beta \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\gamma \hat{\mathrm{k}}\end{aligned}  \quad\left| \begin{array}{ccc}-\mathrm{t} & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & -\mathrm{t} & 1 \\ 1 & 1 & -\mathrm{t}\end{array} \right|=0  \begin{array}{ll}\vec{u} . \vec{w}=0=\alpha+\beta-2 \gamma & t=-1 \text{ or } 2 \\ (\vec{v} . \vec{w}) \times \vec{v}=\vec{u} \times \vec{v} & t=-1 \\ \vec{w}|\vec{v}|^2-0=\vec{w} & \alpha+\beta+\gamma=0 \\ |\vec{v}|=1(P) & t=2 \\ & \alpha=\beta=\gamma\end{array} \begin{aligned} & \text{ Also, } \vec{u} \times \vec{v}=\vec{w} \\ & |\vec{u}||\vec{v}|=|\vec{w}| \\ & \Rightarrow|\vec{u}|=|\vec{w}|=\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}$
Case-1:
 \begin{aligned}
& $\mathrm{t}=$2 \\
& \alpha=\beta=\gamma \\
& \alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=6 \\
& \alpha=\sqrt{2},-\sqrt{2} \\
& $\text{ (S) } \mathrm{t}+$3=5
\end{aligned}$
Case-2:
$\begin{aligned}
& $\mathrm{t}=$-1 \\
& \alpha+\beta+\gamma=0 \\
& \alpha+\beta-2 \gamma=0 \\
& \gamma=0, \alpha=-\beta \\
& ($\mathrm{Q}$) \alpha=\sqrt{3}, \gamma^2=0, \beta=-\sqrt{3} \\
& ($\mathrm{R}$) \alpha=\sqrt{3}(\gamma+\beta)^2=\beta^2=3 \\
& ($\mathrm{P}$) \rightarrow(2),($\mathrm{Q}$) \rightarrow(1),($\mathrm{R}$) \rightarrow(4),($\mathrm{S}$) \rightarrow(5)
\end{aligned}

26016.text: Two inductors ${L}_{i}$ (inductance $1mH$, internal resistance $3Ω$ ) and ${L}_{2}$ (inductance $2mH$, internal resistance $4Ω$ ), and a resistor $R$(resistance $12Ω$ ) are all connected in parallel across a $5V$ battery. The circuit is switched on at time $t = 0$. The ratio of the maximum current $\left(\dfrac{{I}_{max}}{{I}_{min}}\right)$ drawn from the battery is:
26016.sol:
Initally, the inductances will offer infinite resistance and the current will be maximum.

${I}_{max} = \dfrac{ε}{R} = \dfrac{5}{12}A$ (Initially at t = 0)

Upon reaching steady state, the inductances will act as pure resistors and hence the current will be minimum.
${I}_{min} = \dfrac{ε}{{R}_{eq}} = ε\left(\dfrac{1}{{r}_{1}} + \dfrac{1}{{r}_{2}} + \dfrac{1}{R}\right)$ (Finally in steady state)
$= 5\left(\dfrac{1}{3} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{12}\right)$
$= \dfrac{10}{3}A$
$\dfrac{{I}_{max}}{{I}_{min}} = 8$

Statement I:- Dipole moment is a vector quantity and by convention it is depicted by a small arrow with tail on the negative centre and head pointing towards the positive centre.

Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
27817.sol:
Dipole moment is a vector quantity and by convention it is depicted by a small arrow with tail on the negative centre and head pointing towards the positive centre. But in chemistry presence of dipole moment is represented by the crossed arrow put on Lewis structure of the molecule. The cross is on positive end and arrow head is on negative end. So, statement I is incorrect.

The crossed arrow of the dipole moment symbolises the direction of the shift of electron density in the molecules. So, statement II is correct.

Hence the correct option is B

30414.text:
Consider the following compounds

Arrange these compounds in the increasing order of reactivity with nitrating mixture.
30414.sol:
Electrophilic aromatic nitration reactivity depends on the electronic effects of substituents.
Compound a (chlorobenzene) has a weakly deactivating chlorine group.
Compound b (nitrobenzene) has a strongly electron-withdrawing nitro group, making it significantly deactivated.
Compound c (anisole) has an electron-donating methoxy group, making it highly activated.
In order of increasing reactivity with nitrating mixture: nitrobenzene (b) is least reactive due to strong deactivation, chlorobenzene (a) is moderately reactive, and anisole (c) is most reactive due to activation.
The increasing order is b < a < c.

30734.subject: Chemistry
30734.text: The first and second ionization constants of a weak dibasic acid $H_2 A$ are $8.1 \times 10^{-8}$ and $1.0 \times 10^{-13}$ respectively. $0.1$ mol of $H_2 A$ was dissolved in $1$ L of $0.1$ M HCl solution. The concentration of $HA^-$ in the resultant solution is:
30734.sol:
Given:
Weak dibasic acid $H_2A$ with $K_{a1} = 8.1 \times 10^{-8}$ and $K_{a2} = 1.0 \times 10^{-13}$
Initial concentration: $[H_2A]_0 = 0.1\text{ M}$
The solution also contains $0.1\text{ M HCl}$, which dissociates completely to give $[H^+]_0 = 0.1\text{ M}$.

The main source of $HA^-$ is the first dissociation:
$H_2A \rightleftharpoons H^+ + HA^-$

Let $x$ be the amount of $H_2A$ that dissociates. Then at equilibrium:
$[H_2A] = 0.1 - x$
$[H^+] = 0.1 + x$
$[HA^-] = x$

Applying the equilibrium expression:
$K_{a1} = \dfrac{[H^+][HA^-]}{[H_2A]}$

$8.1 \times 10^{-8} = \dfrac{(0.1 + x)(x)}{0.1 - x}$

Since $K_{a1}$ is very small and the common $H^+$ ion from HCl suppresses dissociation, $x \ll 0.1$. Hence:
$0.1 - x \approx 0.1$ and $0.1 + x \approx 0.1$

$8.1 \times 10^{-8} \approx \dfrac{(0.1)(x)}{0.1} = x$

Therefore:
$[HA^-] = x = 8.1 \times 10^{-8}\text{ M}$

The second dissociation ($K_{a2} = 1.0 \times 10^{-13}$) is negligible compared to the first, so the $HA^-$ consumed in that step is insignificant.

Hence, the correct option is $(3)\ 8.1 \times 10^{-8}\text{ M}$.

34753.text: Let the slope of the tangent to a curve $y = f\left(x\right) at \left(x, y\right) be given by $2tanx$\left(cosx - y\right)$. if the curve passes through the point $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}, 0\right)$, then the value of ${∫}_{0}^{\dfrac{\pi}{2}}ydx$ is equal to

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2tanxcosx - 2tanx \cdot y$

Passes through $\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}, 0\right)$

So, $f\left(x\right) = 2cosx - 2\sqrt{2}\cos^{2}x$: Required curve

$∫ f\left(x\right)g\left(x\right)dx = f\left(x\right) ∫ g\left(x\right)dx - ∫ \left(f ' \left(x\right) ∫ g\left(x\right)dx\right)dx$

Let $xtanx + 1 = p$

$⇒ \left(x{sec}^{2}x + tanx\right)dp = dx$

$= {x}^{2} ∫ \dfrac{dp}{{p}^{2}} - ∫ \left(2x ∫ \dfrac{dp}{{p}^{2}}\right)dx$

$= \dfrac{- {x}^{2}}{( xtanx + 1 )} + ∫ \dfrac{2x}{xtanx + 1}dx$

Let ${I}_{1} = 2 ∫ \dfrac{x}{xtanx + 1}dx$

$= 2 ∫ \dfrac{xcosx}{xsinx + cosx}dx$

Let $xsinx + cosx = t$

$⇒ ( xcosx + sinx - sinx ) dx = dt$

$⇒ ( xcosx ) dx = dt$

$= 2 ∫ \dfrac{dt}{t} = 2logt + c$

$= 2log | xsinx + cosx | + c$

$∴ ∫ \dfrac{{x}^{2}\left(x{sec}^{2}x + tanx\right)}{( xtanx + 1{)}^{2}}dx$

$= \dfrac{- {x}^{2}}{xtanx + 1} + 2log | xsinx + cosx | + c$

But $I ( 0 ) = 0$

$⇒ c = 0$

Also,$I\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = - \dfrac{{\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)}^{2}}{\dfrac{\pi}{4} \times 1 + 1} + 2log\left|\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + \dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right|$

$= {\log}_{e}\dfrac{( \pi + 4{)}^{2}}{32} - \dfrac{{\pi}^{2}}{4 ( \pi + 4 )}$

Hence, this is the correct option.

36544.subject: Mathematics
36544.text: A coin is tossed $8$ times. If the probability that exactly $4$ heads appear in the first six tosses and exactly $3$ heads appear in the last five tosses is $p$, then $96p$ is equal to _____.
36544.sol:
Let the outcomes of the $8$ tosses be denoted by $X_1, X_2, X_3, X_4, X_5, X_6, X_7, X_8$.

Let $A$ be the number of heads in the first $3$ tosses ($X_1, X_2, X_3$).
Let $B$ be the number of heads in the next $3$ tosses ($X_4, X_5, X_6$).
Let $C$ be the number of heads in the last $2$ tosses ($X_7, X_8$).

According to the given conditions:
Number of heads in the first six tosses: $A + B = 4$
Number of heads in the last five tosses: $B + C = 3$

Since $C$ is the number of heads in $2$ tosses, $C \le 2$. Thus, $B = 3 - C \ge 1$. Also, $B \le 3$.
The possible values for $B$ are $1, 2, 3$. We analyze each case:

Case 1: $B = 1$
Then $C = 2$ and $A = 3$.
Number of ways = $^{3}C_{3} \times ^{3}C_{1} \times ^{2}C_{2} = 1 \times 3 \times 1 = 3$

Case 2: $B = 2$
Then $C = 1$ and $A = 2$.
Number of ways = $^{3}C_{2} \times ^{3}C_{2} \times ^{2}C_{1} = 3 \times 3 \times 2 = 18$

Case 3: $B = 3$
Then $C = 0$ and $A = 1$.
Number of ways = $^{3}C_{1} \times ^{3}C_{3} \times ^{2}C_{0} = 3 \times 1 \times 1 = 3$

Total number of favorable outcomes = $3 + 18 + 3 = 24$
Total number of possible outcomes for $8$ coin tosses = $2^8 = 256$

The probability $p$ is given by:
$p = \dfrac{24}{256} = \dfrac{3}{32}$

We need to find the value of $96p$:
$96p = 96 \times \dfrac{3}{32} = 3 \times 3 = 9$

Answer: $9$

$= \sqrt{9 - 4}\left(9 - 1\right)$

37986.text: If the shortest distance between the lines $\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{- 3}$ and $\dfrac{x - \lambda}{2} = \dfrac{y + 1}{4} = \dfrac{z - 2}{- 5}$ is $\dfrac{6}{\sqrt{5}}$, then the sum of all possible values of $\lambda$ is :
37986.sol:
$\dfrac{x - 4}{1} = \dfrac{y + 1}{2} = \dfrac{z}{- 3}$

$\dfrac{x - \lambda}{2} = \dfrac{y + 1}{4} = \dfrac{z - 2}{- 5}$

The shortest distance between the lines
$= \left|\dfrac{( \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} ) \cdot \left(\overset{\to}{{d}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{d}_{2}}\right)}{\left|\overset{\to}{{d}_{1}} \times \overset{\to}{{d}_{2}}\right|}\right|$

$a ≡ \left(4, - 1, 0\right), b ≡ \left(\lambda, - 1, 2\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} = \left(4\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j}\right) - \left(\lambda\overset{^}{i} - \overset{^}{j} + 2\overset{^}{k}\right)$

$⇒ \overset{\to}{a} - \overset{\to}{b} = \left(4 - \lambda\right)\overset{^}{i} - 2\overset{^}{k}$

So, the shortest distance is given by,

$D = \left|\dfrac{\left|\begin{cases}\lambda - 4 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & 2 & - 3 \\ 2 & 4 & - 5\end{cases}\right|}{\left|\begin{cases}\overset{^}{i} & \overset{^}{j} & \overset{^}{k} \\ 1 & 2 & - 3 \\ 2 & 4 & - 5\end{cases}\right|}\right|$

$⇒ D = \left|\dfrac{( \lambda - 4 ) ( - 10 + 12 ) - 0 + 2 ( 4 - 4 )}{| 2\overset{^}{i} - 1\overset{^}{j} + 0\overset{^}{k} |}\right|$

$⇒ \dfrac{6}{\sqrt{5}} = \left|\dfrac{2 ( \lambda - 4 )}{\sqrt{5}}\right|$

$⇒ 3 = | \lambda - 4 |$

$⇒ \lambda - 4 = \pm 3$

$⇒ \lambda = 7, 1$

So, sum of all possible values of $\lambda$ is $8$.

38378.subject: Mathematics
38378.text:
Let $\frac{\pi}{2}<\theta<\pi$ and $\cot \theta=-\frac{1}{2 \sqrt{2}}$. Then the value of
$\sin \left(\frac{15 \theta}{2}\right)(\cos 8 \theta+\sin 8 \theta)+\cos \left(\frac{15 \theta}{2}\right)(\cos 8 \theta-\sin 8 \theta)$
is equal to
38378.sol:
Expanding and regrouping:
$\sin\frac{15\theta}{2}(\cos 8\theta + \sin 8\theta) + \cos\frac{15\theta}{2}(\cos 8\theta - \sin 8\theta)$
$= \left(\cos\frac{15\theta}{2}\cos 8\theta + \sin\frac{15\theta}{2}\sin 8\theta\right) + \left(\sin\frac{15\theta}{2}\cos 8\theta - \cos\frac{15\theta}{2}\sin 8\theta\right)$
$= \cos\left(8\theta - \frac{15\theta}{2}\right) + \sin\left(\frac{15\theta}{2} - 8\theta\right) = \cos\frac{\theta}{2} - \sin\frac{\theta}{2}$.
From $\cot\theta = -\frac{1}{2\sqrt{2}}$: $\sin\theta = \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3}$, $\cos\theta = -\frac{1}{3}$.
$\left(\cos\frac{\theta}{2} - \sin\frac{\theta}{2}\right)^2 = 1 - \sin\theta = 1 - \frac{2\sqrt{2}}{3} = \frac{(\sqrt{2}-1)^2}{3}$.
Since $\frac{\pi}{4} < \frac{\theta}{2} < \frac{\pi}{2}$, $\sin\frac{\theta}{2} > \cos\frac{\theta}{2}$, so the value is $\frac{1-\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}$.

38510.text: Let $\overset{\to}{OA} = \overset{\to}{a}, \overset{\to}{OB} = 12\overset{\to}{a} + 4\overset{\to}{b}$ and $\overset{\to}{OC} = \overset{\to}{b}$, where $O$ is the origin. If $S$ is the parallelogram with adjacent sides $OA$ and $OC$, then $\dfrac{areaofthequadrilateralOABC}{areaofS}$ is equal to _____
38510.sol:
Area of parallelogram, $S = | \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} |$

Area of quadrilateral = Area $\left(∆ OAB\right) +$Area $\left(∆ OBC\right)$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} { | \overset{\to}{a} \times ( 12\overset{\to}{a} + 4\overset{\to}{b} ) | + | \overset{\to}{b} \times ( 12\overset{\to}{a} + 4\overset{\to}{b} ) | }$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} { | 4\overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} | + | 12\overset{\to}{b} \times \overset{\to}{a} | }$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} { 4 | \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} | + 12 | \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} | }$

$= \dfrac{16}{2} | \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} |$

$= 8 | ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) |$

Ratio $= \dfrac{8 | ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) |}{| ( \overset{\to}{a} \times \overset{\to}{b} ) |} = 8$

38942.subject: Physics
38942.text: In hydrogen atom spectrum, $(R \rightarrow$ Rydberg's constant $)$ A. the maximum wavelength of the radiation of Lyman series is $\frac{4}{3 R}$ B. the Balmer series lies in the visible region of the spectrum C. the minimum wavelength of the radiation of Paschen series is $\frac{9}{R}$ D. the minimum wavelength of Lyman series is $\frac{5}{4 R}$ Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
38942.sol:
A. Maximum wavelength of Lyman series ($n=1$ to $n=2$):
$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(1 - \frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{3R}{4}$
$\lambda = \frac{4}{3R}$ TRUE

B. The Balmer series lies in the visible region of the spectrum. TRUE

C. Minimum wavelength of Paschen series ($n=3$ to $n=\infty$):
$\frac{1}{\lambda'} = R\left(\frac{1}{9}\right)$
$\lambda' = \frac{9}{R}$ TRUE

D. Minimum wavelength of Lyman series ($n=1$ to $n=\infty$):
$\frac{1}{\lambda} = R\left(1\right)$
$\lambda = \frac{1}{R}$, NOT $\frac{5}{4R}$ FALSE

So A, B and C are correct.

39138.text: In the circuit shown, the energy stored in the capacitor is $n\mu J$. The value of $n$ is _____.
39138.sol:
The capacitor works as an open circuit in the given configuration.

The potential difference between the two plates of the capacitor will be the difference across the resistors having resistances $3Ω and 4Ω$.

Hence, the potential difference $\left(∆ V\right)$ across the capacitor can be calculated as follows:

$\begin{cases}\DeltaV & = & \left(\dfrac{4}{6} \times 12 - \dfrac{3}{12} \times 12\right)V \\ & = & 5V\end{cases}$

The formula to calculate the energy stored in the capacitor is given by

$U = \dfrac{1}{2}C ( ∆ V{)}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) to calculate the required energy stored.

$\begin{cases}U & = & \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6\mu F \times {\left(5V\right)}^{2} \\ & = & 75\mu J\end{cases}$

39145.text: A $600pF$ capacitor is charged by $200V$ supply. It is then disconnected from the supply and is connected to another uncharged $600pF$ capacitor. Electrostatic energy lost in the process is _____ $\mu J$.
39145.sol:
The formula to calculate the initial energy stored in the first capacitor is given by

${U}_{i} = \dfrac{1}{2}C{V}^{2} . . . \left(1\right)

The formula$ to calculate the final energy stored when two capacitors are connected is given by

\begin{cases}{U}_{f} & = & $\dfrac{1}{2}$C{$\left(\dfrac{V}{2}$\right)$}^{2} \times 2 \\ & = & \dfrac{1}{4}C{V}^{2} . . . \left(2\right)\end{cases}$

Subtract equation (2) from equation (1) to obtain the energy loss $\left(∆ U\right)$.

$\begin{cases}∆ U & = & \dfrac{1}{2}C{V}^{2} - \dfrac{1}{4}C{V}^{2} \\ & = & \dfrac{C{V}^{2}}{4} . . . \left(3\right)\end{cases}$

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (3) to calculate the required loss.

$\begin{cases}∆ U & = & \dfrac{600 \times {10}^{- 12} \times ( 200{)}^{2}}{4}J \\ & = & 6\mu J\end{cases}$

39338.text: A thin rod of mass $0 . 9kg$ and length $1m$ is suspended, at rest, from one end so that it can freely oscillate in the vertical plane. A particle of move $0 . 1kg$ moving in a straight line with velocity $80m{s}^{- 1}$ hits the rod at its bottom most point and sticks to it (see figure). The angular speed (in $rad{s}^{- 1}$) of the rod immediately after the collision will be …………
39338.sol:
Given,

Mass of the rod, $M = 0 . 9kg$

Mass of particle, $m = 0 . 1kg$

Length of the rod, $l = 1m$

Velocity of particle, $v = 80m{s}^{- 1}$

No external torque acting on the system of rod and particle, so angular momentum of system about the suspension is conserved, i.e.; ${L}_{i} = {L}_{f}$

$⇒ mvl = I\omega . . . ( 1 )$

Where, $I$ is the momentum of inertia of rod and particle system, $\omega$ is the angular velocity of system just after the collision.

$⇒ mvl = \left(\dfrac{M{l}^{2}}{3} + m{l}^{2}\right)\omega . . . ( 2 )$

Substitute the values in equation (2)

$⇒ 0 . 1 \times 80 \times 1 = \left(\dfrac{0 . 9 \times ( 1{)}^{2}}{3} + 0 . 1 \times ( 1{)}^{2}\right) \times \omega$

$\omega = 20rad{s}^{- 1}$

39355.text: A man (mass $= 50kg$ ) and his son (mass $= 20kg$ ) are standing on a frictionless surface facing each other. The man pushes his son so that he starts moving at a speed of $0.70m{s}^{- 1}$ with respect to the man. The speed of the man with respect to the surface is:
39355.sol:
By conservation of linear momentum,

$\overset{\to}{P}i = \overset{\to}{P}f$

Where $\overset{\to}{P}i$ and $\overset{\to}{P}f$ are initial and final momentum of system (boy + man)

Now, $0 = {m}_{b}\overset{\to}{v}b + {m}_{m}\overset{\to}{v}m$......(i)

${v}_{b} =$ velocity of boy w.r.t. ground

${v}_{m} =$ velocity of man w.r.t. ground

$\overset{\to}{v}bm =$ velocity of boy w.r.t. man

So, $\overset{\to}{v}bm = \overset{\to}{v}b - \overset{\to}{v}m$

or $\overset{\to}{v}b = \overset{\to}{v}bm + \overset{\to}{v}m$

or $\overset{\to}{v}b = 0 . 7 + \overset{\to}{v}m$ ........(ii)

From equation (i) and (ii),

$0 = 20\left(0 . 7 + \overset{\to}{v}m\right) + 50\overset{\to}{v}m$

$\overset{\to}{v}m = - \dfrac{14}{70} = - 0 . 20m{s}^{- 1}$

Negative sign shows velocity of man is opposite to boy.

Kinetic energy $= \dfrac{1}{2}\dfrac{M}{10}\left({V}_{T}^{2} + {V}_{r}^{2}\right) = \dfrac{M}{20}\left(81\dfrac{{GM}_{e}}{2R} + 100{u}^{2} - 100\dfrac{{GM}_{e}}{R}\right)$

41177.text:
This question has Statement-1 and Statement-2. Of the four choices given after the Statements, choose the one that best describes the two Statements.
Statement 1: The internal energy of a perfect gas is entirely kinetic and depends only on absolute temperature of the gas and not on its pressure or volume.
Statement 2: A perfect gas is heated keeping pressure constant and later at constant volume. For the same amount of heat the temperature of the gas at constant pressure is lower than that at constant volume.
options:
Statement-1 is true, Statement- 2 is true and Statement $-2$ is the correct explanation of Statement-1.

Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is false.

Statement-1 is true, Statement-2 is true but Statement-2 is not the correct explanation of Statement-1.

Statement-1 is false, Statement-2 is true.
41177.sol:
Internal energy of a system is the energy possessed by the system due to molecular motion and molecular configuration. Internal energy $u=u_k+u_p$ For an ideal gas there is no molecular attraction $\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{p}}=0$
$\therefore$ Internal energy $\mathrm{u}=\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{k}}$ (i.e., internal kinetic energy)
and $\mathrm{u}=\mathrm{u}_{\mathrm{k}}=\frac{3}{2} \mu \mathrm{RT}$
At constant pressure $(\Delta \mathrm{Q})_{\mathrm{P}}=\mu \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{p}} \Delta \mathrm{T}$
At constant volume $(\Delta \mathrm{Q})_{\mathrm{v}}=\mu \mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{v}} \Delta \mathrm{T}$
As C $_{\mathrm{P}}>\mathrm{C}_{\mathrm{V}} \quad \therefore \quad(\Delta \mathrm{T})_{\mathrm{P}} < (\Delta \mathrm{T})_{\mathrm{V}}$

41564.text: Magnetic fields at two points on the axis of a circular coil at a distance of $0 . 05m$ and $0 . 2m$ from the centre are in the ratio $8: 1$. The radius of coil is _______ .
41564.sol:
We know, the magnetic field on the axis of a current carrying circular ring is given by

$B = \dfrac{{\mu}_{0}}{4\pi}\dfrac{2NIA}{{\left({R}^{2} + {x}^{2}\right)}^{3 / 2}}$

$∴ \dfrac{{B}_{1}}{{B}_{2}} = \dfrac{8}{1} = {\left[\dfrac{{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2}}{{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}}\right]}^{3 / 2}$

$4\left[{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}\right] = \left[{R}^{2} + {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2}\right]$

$4{R}^{2} - {R}^{2} = {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2} - 4 \times {\left(0 . 05\right)}^{2}$

$4{R}^{2} - {R}^{2} = {\left(0 . 2\right)}^{2} - {\left(0 . 1\right)}^{2}$

$3{R}^{2} = 0 . 3 \times 0 . 1$

${R}^{2} = {\left(0 . 1\right)}^{2} ⇒ R = 0 . 1$

41677.subject: Physics
41677.text:
A solenoid has a core made of material with relative permeability $400$. The magnetic field produced in the interior of solenoid is $1.0$ T. The magnetic intensity in SI units is $\alpha \times 10^5$. The value of $\alpha$ is ______.
(Free space permeability $\mu_0=4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ SI units.)
41677.sol:
The magnetic field $B$ inside the solenoid is related to the magnetic intensity $H$ by the formula:

$B = \mu H = \mu_0 \mu_r H$

Rearranging for $H$, we get:

$H = \dfrac{B}{\mu_0 \mu_r}$

Substituting the given values ($B = 1.0$ T, $\mu_r = 400$, and $\mu_0 = 4\pi \times 10^{-7}$ T m/A):

$H = \dfrac{1.0}{4\pi \times 10^{-7} \times 400}$

$H = \dfrac{1.0}{1600\pi \times 10^{-7}}$

$H = \dfrac{1}{16\pi \times 10^{-5}}$

$H = \dfrac{1}{16\pi} \times 10^5$ A/m

Comparing this with the given expression $H = \alpha \times 10^5$, we find:

$\alpha = \dfrac{1}{16\pi}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{16\pi}$

46054.text: A choke is preferred to a resistance for limiting current in AC circuit because
options: there is no wastage of power
choke is a good absorber of heat
46054.sol:
In an AC circuit, the coil of high inductance and negligible resistance used to control current, is called the choke coil. The power factor of such a coil is given by
$\cos \phi=\frac{R}{\sqrt{R^2+\omega^2 L^2}}$
$=\frac{R}{\omega L} \quad($ as $R \ll \lt \omega L)$
As $R \ll \omega L, \cos \phi$ is very small. Thus, the power absorbed by the coil is very small. The only loss of energy is due to hysteresis in the iron core, which is much less than the loss of energy in the resistance that can also reduce the current if placed instead of the choke coil.

Since, $R$ less on the plane r$\cdot(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathbf{j}}+\hat{\mathbf{k}})=1$ Therefore, $\begin{array}{ll} {\left[\left(\frac{\lambda}{2}+1\right) \hat{\mathbf{i}}+\left(\frac{\lambda}{2}\right) \hat{\mathrm{j}}+\left(3+\frac{\lambda}{2}\right) \hat{\mathbf{k}}\right] \cdot(\hat{\mathbf{i}}+\hat{\mathrm{j}}+\hat{\mathrm{k}})} & =1 \\ \Rightarrow \left(\frac{\lambda}{2}+1+\frac{\lambda}{2}+3+\frac{\lambda}{2}\right) \\ \Rightarrow \lambda=-2 \end{array} \\ So, the position vector of $ Q$ is $(\hat{$\mathbf{i}$}+3 \hat{$\mathbf{k}$})-2(\hat{$\mathbf{i}$}+\hat{$\mathbf{j}$}+\hat{$\mathbf{k}$})=-\hat{$\mathbf{i}$}-2 \hat{$\mathbf{j}$}+\hat{$\mathbf{k}$}

55769.subject: Chemistry
55769.text: Which of the following order of dipole moment for stated molecules is correct?
55769.sol:
$\text{BF}_3$ has a symmetrical trigonal planar geometry, so its net dipole moment is zero.

In $\text{NH}_3$, the N-H bond dipoles and the lone pair dipole are in the same direction, which add up to give a high dipole moment.

In $\text{NF}_3$, the N-F bond dipoles and the lone pair dipole are in opposite directions, which partially cancel each other, resulting in a lower dipole moment than $\text{NH}_3$.

Therefore, the correct order of dipole moment is $\text{NH}_3 > \text{NF}_3 > \text{BF}_3$.

Answer: $\text{NH}_3 > \text{NF}_3 > \text{BF}_3$

56616.subject: Chemistry
56616.text: Which of the following prediction is correct when the transition metal ion is colourless?
56616.sol:
The colour of transition metal ions is primarily due to d-d transitions, which require the presence of partially filled d-orbitals.

When the d-orbitals are completely empty (d^0$ configuration, e.g., $Sc^{3+}$, $Ti^{4+}$) or completely filled (d^{10}$ configuration, e.g., $Zn^{2+}$, $Cu^+$), d-d transitions are not possible.

In both $d^0$ and $d^{10}$ configurations, there are no unpaired electrons. Therefore, a transition metal ion is colourless when it contains 0 unpaired electrons.

Answer: it contains 0 unpaired electrons

58604.subject: Chemistry
58604.text: What is the number of electrons gained by Cl atom when $n$ mole of $\text{ClO}_4^-$ is transformed into $n$ mole of $\text{ClO}_2^-$ ion?
58604.sol:
Let the oxidation state of Cl in $\text{ClO}_4^-$ be $x$.

$x + 4(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow x = +7$

Let the oxidation state of Cl in $\text{ClO}_2^-$ be $y$.

$y + 2(-2) = -1 \Rightarrow y = +3$

The change in oxidation state of Cl is from $+7$ to $+3$. This means each Cl atom gains $4$ electrons during the transformation.

For $1$ mole of $\text{ClO}_4^-$, $4$ moles of electrons are gained.

Therefore, for $n$ moles of $\text{ClO}_4^-$, the number of moles of electrons gained is $4n$.

Answer: $4n$

58636.subject: Chemistry
58636.text: Which metal in following compounds is not present in fractional oxidation state?
58636.sol:
The oxidation state of the metal is evaluated for each compound to identify which one is not fractional.

A) For $\mathrm{Fe}_3\mathrm{O}_4$, the oxidation state $x$ satisfies $3x + 4(-2) = 0$, yielding $x = +8/3$, which is fractional.

B) Similarly, for $\mathrm{Mn}_3\mathrm{O}_4$, $3x + 4(-2) = 0$ gives $x = +8/3$, a fractional value.

C) For $\mathrm{Pb}_3\mathrm{O}_4$, the same equation $3x + 4(-2) = 0$ results in $x = +8/3$, also fractional.

D) In $\mathrm{Na}_2\mathrm{S}_4\mathrm{O}_6$, sodium has a fixed oxidation state of $+1$, while sulfur's state from $2(+1) + 4x_\text{S} + 6(-2) = 0$ is $x_\text{S} = +5/2$ (fractional), but the metal (Na) is not fractional.

Thus, only D has a metal not in a fractional oxidation state.

59108.subject: Chemistry
59108.text: Which of the following is the colligative property of a solution?
59108.sol:
Colligative properties are those properties of a solution that depend only on the number of solute particles and not on their nature.

The four colligative properties are:
1. Relative lowering of vapour pressure
2. Elevation of boiling point
3. Depression of freezing point
4. Osmotic pressure

Vapour pressure, boiling point, and freezing point are not colligative properties themselves; rather, their changes (lowering, elevation, and depression, respectively) are colligative properties. Therefore, osmotic pressure is the only colligative property among the given options.

Answer: osmotic pressure

59116.subject: Chemistry
59116.text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about solubility?
options: The solubility of gases in water usually decreases with increase of temperature.
The solubility of gases in water usually increases with increase in pressure.
The substances having similar inter-molecular forces are likely to be soluble in each other.
Gases like $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{CO}_2$ obey Henry's law
59116.sol:
The solubility of gases in liquids is an exothermic process. According to Le Chatelier's principle, solubility decreases with an increase in temperature.

According to Henry's law, the solubility of a gas in a liquid is directly proportional to the pressure of the gas. Thus, solubility increases with an increase in pressure.

Substances with similar intermolecular forces dissolve in each other, following the principle of 'like dissolves like'.

Henry's law is applicable only to gases that do not react chemically with the solvent. Gases like $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{CO}_2$ react with water to form $\text{NH}_4\text{OH}$ and $\text{H}_2\text{CO}_3$ respectively. Hence, they do not obey Henry's law.

Answer: Gases like $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{CO}_2$ obey Henry's law

59887.text: Which of the following relations is correct for a reaction $\text{S}_{(s)} + \text{O}_{2(g)} \rightarrow \text{SO}_{2(g)}$ ?
59887.sol:
The given reaction is $\text{S}_{(s)} + \text{O}_{2(g)} \rightarrow \text{SO}_{2(g)}$

The relationship between enthalpy change ($\Delta H$) and internal energy change ($\Delta U$) is given by:

$\Delta H = \Delta U + \Delta n_g RT$

where $\Delta n_g$ is the change in the number of moles of gaseous substances.

$\Delta n_g = \text{moles of gaseous products} - \text{moles of gaseous reactants}$

For the given reaction, $\text{SO}_{2}$ is the only gaseous product and $\text{O}_{2}$ is the only gaseous reactant. Solid sulfur ($\text{S}_{(s)}$) is not considered.

$\Delta n_g = 1 - 1 = 0$

Substituting $\Delta n_g = 0$ into the equation:

$\Delta H = \Delta U + (0)RT$

$\Delta H = \Delta U$

Answer: $\Delta H = \Delta U$

60573.subject: Mathematics
60573.text: The area of the region (in sq.units) bounded by the curve $y = 2\sqrt{1 - x^2}$ and the X-axis is _____
60573.sol:
The given curve is $y = 2\sqrt{1 - x^2}$.

Squaring both sides, we get $y^2 = 4(1 - x^2) \Rightarrow x^2 + \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1$.

This represents an ellipse with semi-minor axis $a = 1$ and semi-major axis $b = 2$.

Since $y \ge 0$, the given curve represents the upper half of the ellipse.

The area of the complete ellipse is $\pi a b = \pi(1)(2) = 2\pi$.

Therefore, the area of the upper half of the ellipse is $\dfrac{1}{2}(2\pi) = \pi$.

Alternatively, the area can be found by integration:

Area $= \int_{-1}^{1} 2\sqrt{1 - x^2} dx$

Area $= 2 \left[ \dfrac{x}{2}\sqrt{1 - x^2} + \dfrac{1}{2}\sin^{-1}x \right]_{-1}^{1}$

Area $= 2 \left[ \dfrac{1}{2}\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) - \dfrac{1}{2}\left(-\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) \right] = \pi$ sq. units.

Answer: $\pi$

61273.text: The general solution of the differential equation $x\sin x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + (x\cos x + \sin x)y = \sin x$ is
61273.sol:
The given differential equation is $x\sin x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + (x\cos x + \sin x)y = \sin x$

Observing the left hand side, it can be rewritten using the product rule of differentiation:

$x\sin x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y\dfrac{d}{dx}(x\sin x) = \sin x$

$\dfrac{d}{dx}(xy\sin x) = \sin x$

Integrating both sides with respect to $x$:

$\int \dfrac{d}{dx}(xy\sin x) dx = \int \sin x dx$

$xy\sin x = -\cos x + c$

$xy\sin x + \cos x = c$

Answer: $xy\sin x + \cos x = c$

61327.subject: Mathematics
61327.text: $\mathrm{y}=\mathrm{e}^x(\mathrm{ A} \cos x+\mathrm{B} \sin x)$ is the solution of the differential equation
61327.sol:
The differential equation for $y = e^x(A \cos x + B \sin x)$ can be found by differentiating twice to eliminate the arbitrary constants $A$ and $B$.

Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$:

$\frac{dy}{dx} = e^x(A \cos x + B \sin x) + e^x(-A \sin x + B \cos x) = y + e^x(-A \sin x + B \cos x)$

Differentiating again:

$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{d}{dx}[e^x(-A \sin x + B \cos x)]$

Applying the product rule:

$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{dy}{dx} + e^x(-A \sin x + B \cos x) + e^x(-A \cos x - B \sin x)$

Substituting $e^x(-A \sin x + B \cos x) = \frac{dy}{dx} - y$ and $e^x(-A \cos x - B \sin x) = -y$:

$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} = \frac{dy}{dx} + (\frac{dy}{dx} - y) - y = 2\frac{dy}{dx} - 2y$

The resulting differential equation is:

$\frac{d^2y}{dx^2} - 2\frac{dy}{dx} + 2y = 0$

Final answer: $\boxed{\text{C}}$

63595.text: If events A and B are such that $P(A) = \dfrac{1}{4}$, $P(A \cap B) = \dfrac{1}{10}$ and $P(A/B) = 2P(B/A)$ then $P(B) = $...........

Given $P(A) = \dfrac{1}{4}$ and $P(A \cap B) = \dfrac{1}{10}$

Using the definition of conditional probability:

$P(A/B) = \dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)}$

$P(B/A) = \dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)}$

Substituting these into the given relation $P(A/B) = 2P(B/A)$:

$\dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(B)} = 2\dfrac{P(A \cap B)}{P(A)}$

Since $P(A \cap B) \neq 0$, we can cancel it from both sides:

$\dfrac{1}{P(B)} = \dfrac{2}{P(A)}$

$P(B) = \dfrac{P(A)}{2}$

Substituting $P(A) = \dfrac{1}{4}$:

$P(B) = \dfrac{1}{4 \times 2} = \dfrac{1}{8}$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{8}$

64206.subject: Mathematics
64206.text: If a triangle $ABC$ has vertices $A(1,-6), B(2,-3)$ and $C(3,-2)$, then the coordinates of its orthocenter are....
64206.sol:
Let the vertices of the triangle be $A(1,-6)$, $B(2,-3)$, and $C(3,-2)$.

The slope of the side $BC$ is $m_{BC} = \dfrac{-2 - (-3)}{3 - 2} = 1$.
The altitude from $A$ to $BC$ is perpendicular to $BC$, so its slope is $-1$.
The equation of the altitude from $A(1,-6)$ is:
$y - (-6) = -1(x - 1)$
$x + y = -5$... (i)

The slope of the side $AC$ is $m_{AC} = \dfrac{-2 - (-6)}{3 - 1} = \dfrac{4}{2} = 2$.
The altitude from $B$ to $AC$ is perpendicular to $AC$, so its slope is $-\dfrac{1}{2}$.
The equation of the altitude from $B(2,-3)$ is:
$y - (-3) = -\dfrac{1}{2}(x - 2)$
$2y + 6 = -x + 2$
$x + 2y = -4$... (ii)

The orthocenter is the point of intersection of the altitudes. Solving equations (i) and (ii):
Subtracting (i) from (ii), we get:
$(x + 2y) - (x + y) = -4 - (-5)$
$y = 1$

Substituting $y = 1$ into equation (i):
$x + 1 = -5$
$x = -6$

The coordinates of the orthocenter are $(-6,1)$.

Answer: $(-6,1)$

65118.subject: Mathematics
65118.text: If $\bar{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$ and $\bar{b} = \hat{i} - \hat{k}$, then the point of intersection of the lines $\bar{r} \times \bar{a} = \bar{b} \times \bar{a}$ and $\bar{r} \times \bar{b} = \bar{a} \times \bar{b}$ is
65118.sol:
The given equations of the lines are $\bar{r} \times \bar{a} = \bar{b} \times \bar{a}$ and $\bar{r} \times \bar{b} = \bar{a} \times \bar{b}$.

From the first equation, we can write:
$\bar{r} \times \bar{a} - \bar{b} \times \bar{a} = 0$
$\Rightarrow (\bar{r} - \bar{b}) \times \bar{a} = 0$
This implies that the vector $\bar{r} - \bar{b}$ is parallel to $\bar{a}$. Thus, $\bar{r} = \bar{b} + \lambda \bar{a}$ for some scalar $\lambda$.

Similarly, from the second equation:
$\bar{r} \times \bar{b} - \bar{a} \times \bar{b} = 0$
$\Rightarrow (\bar{r} - \bar{a}) \times \bar{b} = 0$
This implies that the vector $\bar{r} - \bar{a}$ is parallel to $\bar{b}$. Thus, $\bar{r} = \bar{a} + \mu \bar{b}$ for some scalar $\mu$.

At the point of intersection, the position vector $\bar{r}$ must satisfy both conditions:
$\bar{b} + \lambda \bar{a} = \bar{a} + \mu \bar{b}$
$\Rightarrow (\lambda - 1)\bar{a} + (1 - \mu)\bar{b} = 0$

Since $\bar{a} = \hat{i} + \hat{j}$ and $\bar{b} = \hat{i} - \hat{k}$ are non-collinear (linearly independent) vectors, their coefficients must be zero:
$\lambda - 1 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 1$
$1 - \mu = 0 \Rightarrow \mu = 1$

Substituting $\lambda = 1$ into the first equation for $\bar{r}$, we get:
$\bar{r} = \bar{a} + \bar{b}$

Substituting the given vectors $\bar{a}$ and $\bar{b}$:
$\bar{r} = (\hat{i} + \hat{j}) + (\hat{i} - \hat{k}) = 2\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$

Therefore, the point of intersection is $(2, 1, -1)$.

Answer: $(2, 1, -1)$

The radius of the $n$-th Bohr orbit for a hydrogen-like atom is given by $r = r_0 \dfrac{n^2}{Z}$, where $r_0$ is the Bohr radius.

For the ground state of hydrogen, $n = 1$ and $Z = 1$.

$r_H = r_0 \dfrac{1^2}{1} = r_0$

For triply ionized beryllium ($\text{Be}^{+++}$), $Z = 4$. Let its principal quantum number be $n$.

$r_{Be} = r_0 \dfrac{n^2}{4}$

Given that the orbital radii are equal, $r_{Be} = r_H$.

$r_0 \dfrac{n^2}{4} = r_0$

$n^2 = 4$

$n = 2$

Answer: $n = 2$

66348.text: The length of a potentiometer wire is 'L'. A cell of e.m.f. E is balanced at a length $\frac{L}{5}$ from the positive end of the wire. If the length of the wire is increased by $\frac{L}{2}$, the same cell will give balance point at distance ' $x$ '. The value of ' $x$ ' is
66348.sol:
The initial potential gradient for potentiometer wire length $L$ with applied voltage $V_0$ is $k_1 = \frac{V_0}{L}$.

With the cell of e.m.f. $E$ balanced at $\frac{L}{5}$, potentiometer principle gives $E = k_1 \cdot \frac{L}{5} = \frac{V_0}{5}$.

When the wire length increases to $\frac{3L}{2}$ with unchanged $V_0$, the new potential gradient becomes $k_2 = \frac{V_0}{\frac{3L}{2}} = \frac{2V_0}{3L}$.

For the same cell e.m.f. balanced at length $x$: $E = k_2 x = \frac{2V_0}{3L} x$.

Equating both expressions for $E$:

$\frac{V_0}{5} = \frac{2V_0}{3L} x$

Canceling $V_0$ and solving yields $x = \frac{3L}{10}$.

The new balance point occurs at $\frac{3L}{10}$.

Correct option: C

The kinetic energy of an ideal gas is directly proportional to its absolute temperature.

$E \propto T$

Initial temperature $T_1 = 27^{}^{\circ}\text{C} = 27 + 273 = 300\text{ K}$

Final temperature $T_2 = 177^{}^{\circ}\text{C} = 177 + 273 = 450\text{ K}$

Using the relation $\dfrac{E_1}{T_1} = \dfrac{E_2}{T_2}$:

69166.subject: Physics
69166.text: If the earth suddenly contracts to $\left(\dfrac{1}{3}\right)^{rd}$ of its present size without change in its mass, the ratio kinetic energy of the earth after and before contraction will be (Earth is assumed to be a rotating sphere about itself)
69166.sol:
By conservation of angular momentum, $L_1 = L_2$.

The rotational kinetic energy is given by $K = \dfrac{L^2}{2I}$.

The ratio of final to initial kinetic energy is $\dfrac{K_2}{K_1} = \dfrac{I_1}{I_2}$.

The moment of inertia of a solid sphere is $I = \dfrac{2}{5}MR^2$.

Given $R_2 = \dfrac{R_1}{3}$, we have $I_2 = \dfrac{2}{5}M\left(\dfrac{R_1}{3}\right)^2 = \dfrac{I_1}{9}$.

Therefore, $\dfrac{K_2}{K_1} = \dfrac{I_1}{\dfrac{I_1}{9}} = 9$.

Answer: $9$

69213.subject: Physics
69213.text: Four particles each of mass M are placed at the corners of a square of side L. The radius of gyration of the system about an axis perpendicular to the square and passing through its centre is
69213.sol:
The system consists of four particles of mass $M$ arranged at the corners of a square of side $L$. The rotation axis is perpendicular to the square's plane and passes through its center.

The distance $r$ from each corner to the center is half the diagonal length. The diagonal is $L\sqrt{2}$, so $r = L/\sqrt{2}$.

The moment of inertia for one particle about this axis is $Mr^2 = M(L^2 / 2) = ML^2 / 2$. For four identical particles, the total moment of inertia is $I_{\text{total}} = 4(ML^2 / 2) = 2ML^2$.

The total mass is $M_{\text{total}} = 4M$. The radius of gyration $k$ satisfies $I_{\text{total}} = M_{\text{total}} k^2$, so $2ML^2 = 4M k^2$.

Solving gives $k^2 = L^2 / 2$, hence $k = L / \sqrt{2}$.

The radius of gyration is $L / \sqrt{2}$.

71516.subject: Biology
71516.text: Which of the following is INCORRECT for recurrent apomixis?
options: Embryo sac generally develops from an archesporial cell
Embryo sac develops from other part of the nucellus
Embryo sac develops from megaspore mother cell.
Embryo develops from reduced egg cell
71516.sol:
In recurrent apomixis, both the egg cell and the embryo are diploid because the embryo sac develops without meiosis. This can occur either from the megaspore mother cell (diplospory) or from any other cell of the nucellus (apospory).

Since meiosis does not take place, the egg cell is unreduced (diploid). The development of an embryo from a reduced (haploid) egg cell without fertilization is known as non-recurrent apomixis (haploid parthenogenesis).

Therefore, the statement that the embryo develops from a reduced egg cell is incorrect for recurrent apomixis.

Answer: Embryo develops from reduced egg cell

71521.subject: Biology
71521.text: If the synergid of an ovule contains 24 chromosomes, then what will be the number of chromosomes in its endosperm?
71521.sol:
Synergids are haploid cells present in the embryo sac of an angiosperm.

Thus, the haploid chromosome number is $n = 24$.

The endosperm in angiosperms is formed by triple fusion and is typically triploid (3n$).

Number of chromosomes in the endosperm = 3n = 3 \times 24 = 72$.

Answer: $72$

71572.subject: Biology
71572.text: The kind of passive absorption of anions against the concentration gradient, in order to neutralize the effect of fixed cations in the cell, is called ____.
71572.sol:
Donnan equilibrium is a passive process that accounts for the accumulation of ions against their concentration gradient without the expenditure of metabolic energy (ATP).

When a cell contains fixed, non-diffusible ions (such as proteins or organic molecules with a net charge), it creates an electrical imbalance. To neutralize the effect of these fixed cations or anions, diffusible ions of the opposite charge from the external medium passively diffuse into the cell.

This movement occurs against the concentration gradient but along the electrical gradient, eventually reaching an equilibrium state known as the Donnan equilibrium.

Answer: Donnan equilibrium

72247.subject: Physics
72247.text: For a circular coil of radius $a$, at what distance $x$ along its axis the magnetic field is exactly $\dfrac{1}{27}$ of its value at the center?
72247.sol:
The magnetic field at the center of a circular coil of radius $a$ is given by $B_c = \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2a}$.

The magnetic field at a distance $x$ along the axis is given by $B_x = \dfrac{\mu_0 I a^2}{2(a^2 + x^2)^{3/2}}$.

Given that $B_x = \dfrac{1}{27} B_c$, we have:

$\dfrac{\mu_0 I a^2}{2(a^2 + x^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{1}{27} \left( \dfrac{\mu_0 I}{2a} \right)

\dfrac{a^3}{(a^2 + x^2)^{3/2}} = \dfrac{1}{27}

Taking the cube root on both sides:

\dfrac{a}{\sqrt{a^2 + x^2}} = \dfrac{1}{3}

Squaring both sides:

\dfrac{a^2}{a^2 + x^2} = \dfrac{1}{9}

9a^2 = a² + x²$

$x^2 = 8a^2$

$x = 2\sqrt{2}$ a$

Answer: 2\sqrt{2}$ a

72323.subject: Physics
72323.text: If the length of seconds pendulum on the surface of the earth is 1 m. The length of the seconds pendulum on the surface of the planet is $\left\{g_{planet}=\dfrac{7}{2}g_{earth}\right\}$ {periodic time of the seconds pendulum is same on both planets}
72323.sol:
The time period of a simple pendulum is given by $T = 2\pi \sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}}$.

Since the time period of a seconds pendulum is constant ($T = 2\ s$), we have $\dfrac{l}{g} = \text{constant}$.

$\dfrac{l_{earth}}{g_{earth}} = \dfrac{l_{planet}}{g_{planet}}$

Substituting the given values $l_{earth} = 1\ m$ and $g_{planet} = \dfrac{7}{2}g_{earth}$:

$\dfrac{1}{g_{earth}} = \dfrac{l_{planet}}{\dfrac{7}{2}g_{earth}}$

$l_{planet} = \dfrac{7}{2}\ m$

Answer: $\dfrac{7}{2}\ m$

72428.subject: Physics
72428.text:
The second law of thermodynamics deals with the transfer of
a. only work.
b. momentum.
c. heat.
d. only pressure.
72428.sol:
The second law of thermodynamics establishes the direction of heat transfer and the limitations on converting heat into work. It states that heat cannot spontaneously flow from a colder body to a hotter body without external work being done. It also implies that it is impossible to construct an engine operating in a cycle that completely converts heat from a single reservoir into an equivalent amount of work.

Thus, the second law of thermodynamics primarily deals with the transfer of heat.

Answer: c

79382.subject: Botany
79382.text: Meristematic tissue responsible for increase in girth of tree trunk is:
79382.sol:
Lateral meristem are present along the lateral sides of stem and roots, and are responsible for lateral growth of trees. Intercalary meristem is associated with the growth in length in the middle position, causing internodal elongation. Phellogen also known as cork cambium is the meristematic plant tissue responsible for the formation of the periderm. Apical meristem is involved in the growth region in plants found within the root tips and the tips of the new shoots and leaves.
Related Theory
When plant breeders want to re-generate plants that are virus-free using asexual multiplication (in order to obtain clones of the primary unhealthy plant), they often collect the apical meristem from the infected plant, and cultivate it in appropriate media, so that a new, complete and virus-free plantlets develop. High metabolic processes (Enzyme activity); High concentration of auxin and Cytokinin hormone (Low pH); Cell multiplication very high and plasmodesmata size very small which prevent the movement of the virus from one cell to another cell.

Quality factor is defined at resonance, when, inductive reactance is equal to the capacitive reactance.

84935.sol:
A molecule that can act as genetic material must fulfill the following criteria:
i) It should chemically and structurally be stable.
ii) It should be able to generate its replica (replication).
iii) It should provide the scope for slow mutation that are required for evolution.
iv) It should be able to express itself in the form of Mendelian characters.

The genetic material should be stable enough not to change with different stages of life cycle, ago or with change in physiology of the organism. DNA being more stable is preferred as genetic material, as
a) Free 2'OH of RNA makes it more labile and easily degradable. Therefore DNA in comparison is more stable.
b) Presence of thymine (5 - Methyl uracil) at the place of uracil also confers additional stability to DNA.
c) RNA being unstable mutates at a faster rate.

89919.text: If the area enclosed by ${y}^{2} = 2x$ and ${x}^{2} + 4 + 4x = 4{y}^{2}$ is $k$ square units, then the value of $3k$ is equal to
89919.sol:
Given equation is ${\left(x + 2\right)}^{2} = 4{y}^{2}$ or $x + 2 = 2y$ and $x + 2 = - 2y$

Solving $x + 2 = 2y$ with the equation of the parabola, we get,

${y}^{2} = 2\left(2y - 2\right)$

$⇒ {y}^{2} - 4y + 4 = 0$

$⇒ y = 2$

Hence, the pair of lines are tangent to the parabola.

So, $k = 2\left\{{∫}_{0}^{2}\dfrac{{y}^{2}}{2}dy - {∫}_{0}^{2}\left(2y - 2\right)dy\right\}$

$= 2{\left(\dfrac{{y}^{3}}{6} - {y}^{2} + 2y\right)}_{0}^{2}$

$= 2\left(\dfrac{8}{6}\right) = \dfrac{8}{3}$

$∴ 3k = 8$

$⇒ f\left(T + x\right) + f\left(x\right) = 2$ ... (1)

$⇒ f\left(2T + x\right) + f\left(T + x\right) = 2$ ... (2)

Subtracting (1) from (2)

$f\left(2T + x\right) - f\left(x\right) = 0$

$f\left(2T + x\right) - f\left(x\right) = 0$

Also, $T$ is positive therefore period of $f\left(x\right) = 2T$

They hang together at the end of a spring with a spring constant $k = 200N{m}^{- 1}$. 94082.sol:
Let $A$ be the amplitude, then we have

$kA = mg ⇒ A = \dfrac{mg}{k}$

$A = \dfrac{\text{0.4} \times g}{200}$$= 2cm$

Motion starts from the lower extreme.

${KE}_{max} = \dfrac{1}{2}{m \omega}^{2}{A}^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2} \times \text{0.3} \times \dfrac{k}{m} \times {A}^{2}$

$= \dfrac{1}{2} \times 0.3 \times \dfrac{200}{0.3} \times {\left(\dfrac{2}{100}\right)}^{2}$

$= \text{0.04}J$

$= 40mJ$

94394.text: If the resistivity of pure silicon is $3000Ωm$ and the mobilities of electrons and holes are $0. 12m^{2}V^{- 1}s^{- 1}$ and $0. 045m^{2}V^{- 1}s^{- 1}$ respectively, then what will be the resistivity of a specimen of silicon when ${10}^{19}$ atoms of phosphorous are added per cubic metre?
94394.sol:
The resistivity of pure $S$ is given by

$ρ = \dfrac{1}{σ} = \dfrac{1}{e\left({n}_{e}{μ}_{e} + {n}_{h}{μ}_{h}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{{en}_{1}\left({μ}_{e} + {μ}_{h}\right)}$

or ${n}_{1} = \dfrac{1}{eρ\left({μ}_{e} + {μ}_{n}\right)} = \dfrac{1}{1. 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times 3000 ( 0. 12 + 0. 045 )}$

$= 1. 26 \times {10}^{16}m^{- 3}$

When ${10}^{19}$ atoms of phosphorous (donor atoms of valence five) are added per $m^{3},$ the semiconductor becomes $n$ - type semiconductor.

$∴ {n}_{e} - {n}_{h} \approx {n}_{e} = {N}_{d} = {10}^{19} ∵ {n}_{n} = 1. 26 \times {10}^{16}$

Resitivity $ρ = \dfrac{1}{{n}_{e}{μ}_{e}e} = \dfrac{1}{1. 6 \times {10}^{- 19} \times {10}^{19} \times 0. 12} = 5. 21Ωm$

options: a sort of sexual reproduction by adopting a primitive type of DNA transfer from one bacterium to the other.
95925.sol: The single-celled bacterium reproduces by binary fission where it divides into two identical daughter cells. This process of fission begins when the DNA of the bacteria replicates and divides into two. When the conditions are not suitable, some bacteria produce spores and undergo asexual reproduction. These unicellular organisms also reproduce by transferring DNA which can be either floating in the environment (transformation), when the DNA moves from one bacterium to another through a conjugation tube between them by the process of conjugation.

102936.subject: Physics
102936.text:
A solid uncharged conducting sphere contains a spherical cavity. A point charge $+Q$ is placed off-center inside this cavity. Consider the following four statements:
(I) The induced charge on the inner surface of the cavity is $-Q$ and is distributed uniformly.
(II) The induced charge on the outer surface of the sphere is $+Q$ and is distributed uniformly.
(III) The net electric field inside the solid bulk of the conductor is zero.
(IV) The electric field outside the sphere is radially outward and spherically symmetric.

How many of the given statements are correct?
102936.sol:
The point charge $+Q$ is placed off-center inside the spherical cavity. To maintain a zero electric field inside the solid bulk of the conductor (Statement III is correct), the induced charge $-Q$ on the inner surface of the cavity must distribute non-uniformly to cancel the asymmetric field of the off-center charge (Statement I is incorrect).

The isolated conducting sphere is initially uncharged, so a net charge of $+Q$ is induced on its outer surface. Since the outer surface is perfectly spherical and there is no external electric field, this charge $+Q$ distributes uniformly over the outer surface (Statement II is correct).

Because the charge distribution on the outer surface is uniform and spherical, the electric field outside the sphere behaves as if a point charge $+Q$ is situated at the center of the sphere. Thus, it is radially outward and spherically symmetric (Statement IV is correct).

Therefore, exactly 3 statements are correct.

Answer: 3

103148.subject: Physics
103148.text: A capacitor $C_1$ of $4 \mu\text{F}$ is connected in series with an unknown capacitor $C_2$ across a DC voltage source. The energy stored in $C_1$ is found to be $4$ times the energy stored in $C_2$. The capacitance of $C_2$ is :
103148.sol:
In a series combination, the charge $Q$ on both capacitors is the same.

The energy stored in a capacitor is given by $U = \dfrac{Q^2}{2C}$. This shows that for a constant charge, the energy stored is inversely proportional to the capacitance ($U \propto \dfrac{1}{C}$).

Given that the energy stored in $C_1$ is $4$ times the energy stored in $C_2$ ($U_1 = 4 U_2$), we can write:
$\dfrac{Q^2}{2C_1} = 4 \left(\dfrac{Q^2}{2C_2}\right)$

Simplifying this, we get:
$\dfrac{1}{C_1} = \dfrac{4}{C_2}$

Rearranging for $C_2$ gives:
$C_2 = 4 C_1$

Substituting the given value $C_1 = 4 \mu\text{F}$:
$C_2 = 4 \times 4 \mu\text{F} = 16 \mu\text{F}$

Answer: $16 \mu\text{F}$

104090.subject: Physics
104090.text: The standard household alternating current (AC) supply in India is rated at $220\text{ V}$. What is the peak voltage of this supply?
104090.sol:
The voltage rating given for an AC supply always represents its root mean square (RMS) value. Therefore, the RMS voltage is $V_{rms} = 220\text{ V}$.

The relationship between the peak voltage ($V_0$) and the RMS voltage for a sinusoidal AC wave is given by:
$V_0 = \sqrt{2} \times V_{rms}$

Substituting the given value:
$V_0 = 1.414 \times 220\text{ V} \approx 311\text{ V}$

Thus, the peak voltage of the supply is approximately $311\text{ V}$.

Answer: $311\text{ V}$

114402.text: The limiting molar conductivities ($\Lambda_m^0$) for $\text{HCl}$, $\text{NaCl}$ and $\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}$ are $426 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$, $126 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ and $90 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$ respectively. If the molar conductivity of a $0.001 \text{ M}$ $\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$ solution is $39 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$, the degree of dissociation of acetic acid at this concentration is:
114402.sol:
According to Kohlrausch's law, the limiting molar conductivity of acetic acid ($\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}$) is calculated from the given strong electrolytes as follows:

$\Lambda_m^0(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}) = \Lambda_m^0(\text{CH}_3\text{COONa}) + \Lambda_m^0(\text{HCl}) - \Lambda_m^0(\text{NaCl})$
$\Lambda_m^0(\text{CH}_3\text{COOH}) = 90 + 426 - 126 = 390 \text{ S cm}^2 \text{ mol}^{-1}$

The degree of dissociation ($\alpha$) is given by the ratio of molar conductivity at a given concentration ($\Lambda_m$) to the limiting molar conductivity ($\Lambda_m^0$):

$\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^0}$
$\alpha = \dfrac{39}{390} = 0.1$

The correct degree of dissociation is $0.1$. The distractor $0.01$ arises from a decimal placement error, $10$ from inverting the formula, and $0.08$ from incorrectly adding or subtracting the strong electrolyte values.

Answer: $0.1$

121580.subject: Botany
121580.text:
Read the following statements regarding the characteristics of kingdoms in Whittaker's five-kingdom classification:
I. Kingdom Monera: Prokaryotic cell type, non-cellulosic cell wall, and cellular body organisation.
II. Kingdom Protista: Eukaryotic cell type, cell wall absent in all members, and cellular body organisation.
III. Kingdom Fungi: Eukaryotic cell type, chitinous cell wall, and tissue/organ system body organisation.
IV. Kingdom Plantae: Eukaryotic cell type, cellulosic cell wall, and tissue/organ body organisation.
V. Kingdom Animalia: Eukaryotic cell type, cell wall absent, and tissue/organ/organ system body organisation.

How many of the above statements are correct?
121580.sol:
According to Whittaker's five-kingdom classification:

Statement I is correct: Monera are prokaryotes with a non-cellulosic cell wall and cellular body organisation.

Statement II is incorrect: Protists are eukaryotes with a cellular body organisation, but a cell wall is present in some members (not absent in all).

Statement III is incorrect: Fungi are eukaryotes with a chitinous cell wall, but their body organisation is multicellular/loose tissue, not tissue/organ system.

Statement IV is correct: Plantae are eukaryotes with a cellulosic cell wall and tissue/organ body organisation.

Statement V is correct: Animalia are eukaryotes without a cell wall and possess tissue/organ/organ system body organisation.

Therefore, exactly three statements (I, IV, and V) are correct.

Answer: Three

122032.sol:
In gymnosperms, the strobili bearing microsporophylls and microsporangia are called male strobili, and those bearing megasporophylls with ovules are called female strobili.

In Cycas, male cones and megasporophylls are borne on different trees (dioecious condition). Marchantia is a bryophyte and lacks true strobili, while Equisetum is a homosporous pteridophyte that does not produce distinct male and female cones on trees.

Answer: Pinus

123243.text: What is the difference between the epidermis of a dicot and a monocot leaf?
options: The epidermis of a dicot leaf has more stomata than a monocot leaf
The epidermis of a monocot leaf has more stomata than a dicot leaf
The epidermis of a monocot leaf is thicker than a dicot leaf
The epidermis of a dicot leaf is thicker than a monocot leaf
123243.sol: The vertical section of a dorsiventral leaf through the lamina shows three main parts, namely, epidermis, mesophyll and vascular system. The epidermis which covers both the upper surface (adaxial epidermis) and lower surface (abaxial epidermis) of the leaf has a conspicuous cuticle. The abaxial epidermis generally bears more stomata than the adaxial epidermis. The latter may even lack stomata. The tissue between the upper and the lower epidermis is called the mesophyll. Mesophyll, which possesses chloroplasts and carry out photosynthesis, is made up of parenchyma. It has two types of cells – the palisade parenchyma and the spongy parenchyma. The adaxially placed palisade parenchyma is made up of elongated cells, which are arranged vertically and parallel to each other. The oval or round and loosely arranged spongy parenchyma is situated below the palisade cells and extends to the lower epidermis. There are numerous large spaces and air cavities between these cells. Vascular system includes vascular bundles, which can be seen in the veins and the midrib. The size of the vascular bundles are dependent on the size of the veins. The veins vary in thickness in the reticulate venation of the dicot leaves. The vascular bundles are surrounded by a layer of thick walled bundle sheath cells. and find the position of xylem in the vascular bundle.

125172.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): In aerobic respiration, oxygen directly participates in the reactions of the Krebs cycle to drive the complete oxidation of pyruvate.

Reason (R): Oxygen acts as the final hydrogen acceptor, driving the whole aerobic process by removing hydrogen from the system.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
125172.sol:
The Assertion is incorrect because oxygen does not directly participate in the Krebs cycle or glycolysis. Its active role is strictly limited to the terminal stage of aerobic respiration (the electron transport system).

The Reason is correct. Although oxygen's participation is limited to the terminal stage, its presence is vital because it acts as the final hydrogen acceptor. By removing hydrogen (protons and electrons) from the system to form water, it drives the entire process of aerobic respiration, allowing the continuous oxidation of NADH back to NAD+.

Therefore, (A) is not correct but (R) is correct.

Answer: (A) is not correct but (R) is correct

125612.subject: Botany
125612.text: During a specific light reaction process in chloroplasts, an excited electron is not transferred to $\text{NADP}^+$ but cycles back to the reaction centre complex via the electron transport chain. Which of the following statements is correct regarding this specific event?
options: It requires the splitting of water to supply continuous electrons.
It occurs in membrane regions that lack the NADP reductase enzyme.
It occurs primarily in grana lamellae where both photosystems are functional.
It results in the simultaneous synthesis of both ATP and $\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+$.
125612.sol:
The process described in the question is cyclic photophosphorylation, where the electron is circulated within Photosystem I (PS I).

This process occurs in the stroma lamellae, which lack both PS II and the NADP reductase enzyme. Because it lacks PS II, there is no photolysis (splitting) of water. The cyclic flow of electrons results only in the synthesis of ATP, not $\text{NADPH} + \text{H}^+$.

Therefore, the correct statement is that it occurs in membrane regions lacking the NADP reductase enzyme.

Answer: It occurs in membrane regions that lack the NADP reductase enzyme.

125825.subject: Botany
125825.text: Why are pollen grains well-preserved as fossils?
options: Because of the presence of cellulose
Because of the presence of sporopollenin
125825.sol: Pollen grains are generally spherical measuring about 25-50 micrometers in diameter. It has a prominent two-layered wall. The hard outer layer called the exine is made up of sporopollenin which is one of the most resistant organic material known. It can withstand high temperatures and strong acids and alkali. No enzyme that degrades sporopollenin is so far known. Pollen grain exine has prominent apertures called germ pores where sporopollenin is absent. Pollen grains are well preserved as fossils because of the presence of sporopollenin. The exine exhibits a fascinating array of patterns and designs. Why do you think the exine should be hard? What is the function of germ pore? The inner wall of the pollen grain is called the intine. It is a thin and continuous layer made up of cellulose and pectin. The cytoplasm of pollen grain is surrounded by a plasma membrane.

126200.subject: Botany
126200.text:
Read the following statements regarding pollination and outbreeding devices:
(I) In some species, pollen release and stigma receptivity are not synchronised to prevent autogamy.
(II) Self-incompatibility is a genetic mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules.
(III) In papaya, male and female flowers are present on the same plant, preventing geitonogamy.
(IV) Geitonogamy is functionally cross-pollination but genetically similar to autogamy.

How many of the above statements are correct?
126200.sol:
Statement (I) is correct: Lack of synchronisation between pollen release and stigma receptivity is an outbreeding device that prevents autogamy.

Statement (II) is correct: Self-incompatibility is a genetically mediated mechanism that prevents self-pollen from fertilising the ovules by inhibiting pollen germination or pollen tube growth in the pistil.

Statement (III) is incorrect: Papaya is a dioecious plant, meaning male and female flowers are present on different plants. This condition prevents both autogamy and geitonogamy. Plants with male and female flowers on the same plant are monoecious (e.g., castor and maize).

Statement (IV) is correct: Geitonogamy involves the transfer of pollen to the stigma of another flower of the same plant. It requires a pollinating agent (making it functionally cross-pollination) but the pollen grains come from the same plant (making it genetically similar to autogamy).

Therefore, three statements (I, II, and IV) are correct.

Answer: Three

129712.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An increase in blood flow to the atria of the heart causes a further increase in blood pressure.
Reason (R): The atria of the heart secrete Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF) which causes vasodilation and acts as a check on the renin-angiotensin mechanism.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A)
Assertion (A) is true but Reason (R) is false
Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true
129712.sol:
An increase in blood flow to the atria of the heart triggers the release of Atrial Natriuretic Factor (ANF). ANF causes vasodilation (dilation of blood vessels) and thereby decreases the blood pressure, rather than increasing it. Therefore, Assertion (A) is false.

The Reason (R) is a correct statement because ANF acts antagonistically to the renin-angiotensin mechanism, serving as a check on it by promoting vasodilation and reducing blood pressure.

Answer: Assertion (A) is false but Reason (R) is true

Assertion (A) is correct because in DNA fingerprinting, the separated DNA fragments are first transferred (blotted) onto synthetic membranes like nitrocellulose or nylon before they are hybridised with a labelled VNTR probe.

Reason (R) is also correct because gel electrophoresis separates DNA fragments based on their size due to the sieving effect of the gel.

132278.subject: Zoology
132278.text: What type of genetic disorder is Thalassemia?
132278.sol: This is also an autosome-linked recessive blood disease transmitted from parents to the offspring when both the partners are unaffected carrier for the gene (or heterozygous). The defect could be due to either mutation or deletion which ultimately results in reduced rate of synthesis of one of the globin chains (α and β chains) that make up haemoglobin. This causes the formation of abnormal haemoglobin molecules resulting into anaemia which is characteristic of the disease. Thalassemia can be classified according to which chain of the haemoglobin molecule is affected. In α Thalassemia, production of α globin chain is affected while in β Thalassemia, production of β globin chain is affected. α Thalassemia is controlled by two closely linked genes HBA1 and HBA2 on chromosome 16 of each parent and it is observed due to mutation or deletion of one or more of the four genes. The more genes affected, the less alpha globin molecules produced. While β Thalassemia is controlled by a single gene HBB on chromosome 11 of each parent and occurs due to mutation of one or both the genes. Thalassemia differs from sickle-cell anaemia in that the former is a quantitative problem of synthesising too few globin molecules while the latter is a qualitative problem of synthesising an incorrectly functioning globin

132710.subject: Zoology
132710.text: Who proposed the idea that evolution of life forms occurred due to the use and disuse of organs?
132710.sol: Even before Darwin, a French naturalist Lamarck had said that evolution of life forms had occurred but driven by use and disuse of organs. He gave the examples of Giraffes who in an attempt to forage leaves on tall trees had to adapt by elongation of their necks. As they passed on this acquired character of elongated neck to succeeding generations, Giraffes, slowly, over the years, came to acquire long necks. Nobody believes this conjecture any more. Is evolution a process or the result of a process? The world we see,inanimate and animate, is only the success stories of evolution. When we describe the story of this world we describe evolution as a process. On the other hand when we describe the story of life on earth, we treat evolution as a consequence of a process called natural selection. We are still not very clear whether to regard evolution and natural selection as processes or end result of unknown processes.

133237.sol: The exaggerated response of the immune system to certain antigens present in the environment is called allergy. Higher vertebrates can distinguish foreign molecules as well as foreign organisms, which is the basis for most experimental immunology. Auto-immune disease occurs when the body attacks self-cells, resulting in damage to the body.

B. Malignant tumorII. Mass of proliferating neoplastic cells that invade tissues
